# Burnly v0.1.37

Cuts the disk and memory cost of a quiet refresh. An unchanged catch-up no longer re-reads stored source history, and collector databases stay open only while a refresh is running.

## Highlights

- **OpenCode reads only what changed.** A catch-up refresh skips assistant messages already stored in the ledger. A session that is still being written keeps a cursor and retries only the unfinished rows, so a later quiet refresh does not range-read the completed tail again. Token growth is still collected when the source cost is only a fraction of a cent below the stored sum. Daily and session totals stay the same as a full collect.
- **Antigravity skips unchanged conversation files.** Incremental refresh stats each conversation and opens the SQLite file only when its length or mtime changed, or when Burnly has no cached usage for it. Unchanged files still contribute the cached usage for the requested dates. The checkpoint stores a path fingerprint, length, mtime, variant, and conversation id. It does not store the path or the conversation text.
- **Refresh jobs close their own SQLite connections.** Collector caches and repair state open when a refresh starts and close when it finishes. The tray keeps a separate read connection, so the panel can load while a collect is in progress. Read connections use a 512 KiB page cache. The reconciliation writer uses 2 MiB. `synchronous=FULL` stays.
- **Old import history is pruned.** After a successful refresh, Burnly deletes `import_runs` older than 14 days in batches of 1000. The newest succeeded row for each source, projection, timezone, and collector profile stays, including when that row is older than 14 days. Recent failures stay. Usage rows are not deleted.
- **Linux compositing trial reverted.** A packaged run kept `libLLVM` and `libnvidia-eglcore` mapped and did not lower idle memory by 100 MB, so Burnly does not set `WEBKIT_DISABLE_COMPOSITING_MODE`. The transparent tray panel is unchanged.

## Privacy

Burnly continues to read usage-only metadata. It selects model identity, token
counters, cost, and generation timestamps. It does not read prompt text,
response content, tool invocations, titles, project paths, or credentials.

## Install

### Linux

Run:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/fikrilal/burnly/releases/latest/download/install-linux.sh | sh
```

For a pinned install of this release:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/fikrilal/burnly/releases/download/v0.1.37/install-linux.sh | BURNLY_VERSION=v0.1.37 sh
```

### Windows Preview

Download the Windows x64 installer from this release:

```text
burnly-v0.1.37-windows-x86_64.exe
```

The Windows preview installer is not Authenticode-signed. Windows may show an
unknown publisher or SmartScreen warning. Only download Burnly from the
official GitHub release and verify the published `SHA256SUMS`. Tauri updater
artifacts remain cryptographically signed.

### macOS Preview

Run:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/fikrilal/burnly/releases/latest/download/install-macos.sh | sh
```

For a pinned install of this release:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/fikrilal/burnly/releases/download/v0.1.37/install-macos.sh | BURNLY_VERSION=v0.1.37 sh
```

Manual `.dmg` installation is also available:

```text
burnly-v0.1.37-macos-aarch64.dmg
burnly-v0.1.37-macos-x86_64.dmg
```

The macOS preview is unsigned and not notarized. If Gatekeeper blocks the
downloaded app, clear quarantine once after copying it to Applications:

```bash
xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Burnly.app
```

## Verification

Local gates cover the OpenCode, Antigravity, connection-lifetime, retention,
and compositing tests. On the packaged Linux AppImage, a second unchanged
catch-up added 12,464,128 read bytes. A refresh after one 49,152-byte
conversation file changed added 49,152 read bytes, and that file's checkpoint
matched the new mtime. About 60 seconds later, cgroup `inactive_file` was
211,939,328 bytes. The compositing variable stays unset.

Release artifacts include `SHA256SUMS`, GitHub build provenance, signed updater
artifacts, `latest.json`, and the `latest-linux.json` compatibility alias.
